items.title: Availability aur nines: 99.9% ka matlab saal mein kitna downtime
items.one_idea: Availability is uptime divided by total time; each extra nine cuts the allowed downtime per year by about 10x (99.9% is about 9 hours, 99.99% about 53 minutes, 99.999% about 5 minutes), and dependencies in a row multiply their availabilities, so the total is lower than any single part.
items.spoken_hook: 99.9% uptime का मतलब: साल में कितनी देर बंद रहेगा?
items.hook_10s: 99.9% uptime का मतलब: साल में कितनी देर बंद रहेगा? अगर तुम्हारा app साल में 9 घंटे बंद रहे, तो वो 99.9% है। और 99.99% में सिर्फ़ 53 मिनट। [frame 0: a 365-day bar with one thin red sliver, label 99.9%]
items.hook_formula: direct_question: the number the viewer has seen on every SLA page, asked as a plain question about it

hook_candidates.text: 99.9% uptime का मतलब: साल में कितनी देर बंद रहेगा?
तुम्हारी payment app साल में कितनी देर बंद रह सकती है?
99.9% uptime में भी साल के करीब 9 घंटे बंद रहता है।

items.visual_idea: One fixed frame: a long 365-day bar with the allowed downtime cut out as a red sliver; stepping 99%, 99.9%, 99.99%, 99.999% shrinks the sliver each time (3.65 days, 8.8 hours, 53 minutes, 5 minutes) on a ladder of cards. Then three boxes in a row (load balancer, app, database) with their availabilities multiplying into a thicker sliver.
items.everyday_anchor: A UPI payment app or IRCTC booking page being down for a few hours on the day you need it: the same 'almost always up' number can still mean a missed payment.
items.example: EXAMPLE (arithmetic shown on screen): 365 days x 24 h = 8,760 h; 0.1% of 8,760 h = 8.76 h (99.9%); 0.01% = 52.6 min (99.99%); 0.001% = 5.26 min (99.999%). Three parts in a row, each EXAMPLE 99.9%: 0.999 x 0.999 x 0.999 = 0.997, so about 26 h of downtime a year.
facts_to_verify: Nines table (High availability page): 99% = 3.7 days/yr, 99.9% = 9 h, 99.99% = 53 min, 99.999% = 5.3 min; the page expresses availability as a percentage of uptime in a given year.
Recompute from 365 days: 0.1% of 8,760 h = 8.76 h; 0.01% = 52.6 min; 0.001% = 5.26 min. Show the arithmetic on screen, round the way the page does.
Availability = uptime / (uptime + downtime) (Wikipedia Availability); unavailability = 1 minus availability.
Series multiplication 0.999^3 = 0.997 is arithmetic (assumes independent failures and every part needed); say so and label the three parts EXAMPLE. Run it and show the real output.

AWS EC2 SLA page: region-level commitment is at least 99.99% Monthly Uptime Percentage across two or more AZs; credits 10% below 99.99%, 30% below 99.0%, 100% below 95.0%. Name it on screen as 'Source: aws.amazon.com' if used; do not claim AWS actually achieves it.
High availability page: scheduled downtime also counts for true HA although many sites exclude it; mention only if time allows.
Do not say any named company runs at a given number of nines.
